## Commits and releases

- Commit identity: human/AI contributors commit as `ai.teammate
  <agent.ai.native@gmail.com>` (history was rewritten to it — set
  `git config user.name ai.teammate` + `git config user.email
  agent.ai.native@gmail.com` repo-locally). Release TAGS from
  `scripts/auto_release.sh` are authored `fa-release-bot[bot]
  <fa-release-bot[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>` — the gh-1172 App pushes
  the annotated tag, so the App identity is what auditability hangs on.
  gh-1402 rule: ANY automation that commits/pushes release-path changes
  (store metadata fixes, release tags/releases) MUST use the fa-release-bot
  GitHub App token — never a PAT, never the default `GITHUB_TOKEN`
  (main's required status checks reject both, #1098).
- Commit subjects: `type(scope): ...` (`feat:`, `fix:`, `fix(example):`,
  `ci:`, `test(providers):`, `refactor(prompts):`).
- Every push to `main` cuts an annotated TAG (`scripts/auto_release.sh`
  via `ci.yml`) — ZERO commits land on main (gh-1522: the retired flow
  pushed a 4-file `chore(release):` bot commit per release). gh-1801: NO
  GitHub Release is created at tag-cut time (an asset-less create
  published an empty `latest` that broke `fa update`): the tag-run
  `binaries` job creates the release DRAFT-first via
  `scripts/release_lazy_draft.sh` (curated CHANGELOG notes via
  `release_notes.sh` + a `release-draft-owner` marker), every leg attaches
  into it, and `release-provenance` publishes + flags `latest` ONLY after
  the signed SHA256SUMS(.sig) is attached — `latest` never points at a
  release that cannot serve `fa update`. The git TAG is the single source
  of truth for versions:
  both pubspecs carry the FIXED `0.0.0-dev` placeholder (a hand-bump fails
  the Static `Version placeholder guard`), `pubspec.lock` never churns, and
  CI stamps the version at the edges: the `publish` job stamps the STAGED
  publish tree (pubspec version + generated changelog section prepend via
  `scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh`, staged version == tag guarded
  pre-upload), store/mobile builds stamp `--build-name/--build-number` from
  the derived tag version, `install_local.sh` stamps `version.txt` from
  `git describe`. CHANGELOG.md is curated-only: PRs add lines under
  `## Unreleased`; the release folds it into the tag's section AT STAGE
  TIME (`scripts/release_notes.sh` preference order: curated `## <version>`
  section → curated `## Unreleased` body → conventional commits since the
  previous tag). The version scheme is `1.0.<counter>` (gh-785: App Store
  Connect approved 1.0.0 and enforces a monotonic
  `CFBundleShortVersionString`, so the pre-promotion `0.1.<counter>`
  train can never upload again). Release checklist: push to main (or the
  `releaseDispatch` dispatch) → watch the ci.yml `release` job cut the tag
  → watch the tag-scoped `publish` + `binaries` + `release-provenance`
  jobs (the release publishes at the provenance step). `fa --version` reads
  the stamped `version.txt` first, the placeholder pubspec second.
- `packages/fa_llm` publishes per `fa_llm-v*` tag via
  `.github/workflows/publish-fa-llm.yml` (OIDC, no secrets). First
  publish of a NEW package is manual — pub.dev OIDC only uploads new
  versions of an existing package (issue #1511): owner runs
  `cd packages/fa_llm && dart pub publish` once, adds the OIDC publisher
  entry on pub.dev, then the workflow takes over. The workflow
  pre-flights the package-exists probe and exits 10 with the
  instructions on 404; see `packages/fa_llm/README.md` §Publishing.
- CLI binaries build per tag (`ci.yml` `binaries` job), attach to the
  GitHub Release (`fa-<os>-<arch>[.exe]`); `installer-smoke` verifies
  installers.
- App builds (`build-mobile.yml`, `build-macos.yml`, manual dispatch):
  Android AAB + iOS IPA on `[self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]`, macOS DMG/ZIP
  signed + notarized, TestFlight via `flutter_app/fastlane`. Optional
  secrets: `APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID/_ISSUER_ID/_KEY_CONTENT`,
  `MACOS_INSTALLER_P12_BASE64/_PASSWORD/MACOS_INSTALLER_CERT_ID`,
  `GOOGLE_SERVICE_INFO_PLIST_BASE64`. Both workflows hard-gate the binary
  on wasm_run FFI exports (`xcrun dyld_info -exports` must list
  `_wire_compile_wasm` — Podfiles force-load + `-exported_symbol` +
  `STRIP_STYLE=non-global`, else white screen on TestFlight). Pods cached
  keyed by `Podfile.lock`. The gate proves FFI exports ONLY — a Dart boot
  crash before the first frame white-screens TestFlight with a green gate
  (issue #544: build 160, boot refactor created the platform env before
  `WidgetsFlutterBinding.ensureInitialized`); boot stage order is pinned by
  `flutter_app/test/boot/app_boot_test.dart`.

## Unreleased

- fix(#1941): the selected CodeMie project now rides EVERY model request.
  The header is baked into `Model.headers` only by the connect-time
  switches (gh-1809), so every other rebuild silently dropped
  `x-codemie-project` — and the backend bills a header-less request against
  the user's DEFAULT project (codemie-code `header-injection.plugin.ts`
  contract): the reported symptom is limit-exhausted from the exhausted
  default project despite picking a budgeted one. Rebuilds now re-resolve
  the project from the saved entry through one helper
  (`projectHeaderForBaseUrl`): the boot folder-state restore (JWT entries
  previously booted header-less — the SSO cookie patch was the only boot
  carrier), the session-resume re-apply (`_buildRestoredModel`), the
  roles-chain failover (`ModelRef.project`, mirroring the #964 authHeader
  leg), the roles-mode `/model` + settings-flow pins, and the generic
  `/provider` switch. The models list (`/llm_models`, SSO + JWT + guided
  setup + entry dispatch) and the quota adapter (dark until pinned) scope
  themselves to the same project, so display and billing can never diverge.
  Tests pin the header VALUE on the wire (real adapter over a fake
  endpoint) for the restored and failed-over models.
- feat(network): private networks created outside the app surface after
  sign-in. `GET /api/networks/mine` (fa_network#16) is synced into the
  wallet after OAuth/dev sign-in and both restore paths — best-effort,
  silent on older backends (404) and any failure, and never destructive.
  Synced memberships keep the server's name/class, preserve local
  passwords/join facts, and land without a password (the endpoint never
  returns one) until the first join. Entering such a network — sidebar,
  ⌘K/⌘3-9, or a restored selection — opens the join sheet prefilled with
  the network id instead of a resume error or endless spinner; joining by
  name now keys the wallet/session by the echoed canonical id and migrates
  legacy name-keyed rows (password + channel keys) instead of duplicating
  them. A malformed `/mine` row is skipped, not the whole list.
- fix(gh-1931): one render per tool call on the non-TUI console. Line mode
  and the headless `-p` log printed every executed call twice — a start row

## Unreleased

- fix(gh-1948): `task_observe` works on a RUNNING background subagent
  instead of crashing with an uncaught `SessionException` on the
  `<parentSessionId>/<agentName>` placeholder. Three legs: the executor
  flushes each child's transcript incrementally at every turn boundary
  (the JSONL exists and grows mid-run — also crash-resilience for
  aborted children), `task_observe` resolves a placeholder handle's real
  session file from the sessions tree (the same `agent: subagent` /
  `parent:` / `id:` header scan the boot adoption uses) and heals the
  handle onto the found path, and every read failure degrades to a
  structured "transcript unavailable" / "no transcript available yet"
  message instead of an uncaught tool error. The child-transcript reader
  rides the transient-ENOENT retry (issue #427) — it reads while the
  executor appends.
- fix(#1941): the selected CodeMie project now rides EVERY model request.

arguments.content:
### What changed
`task_observe` on a RUNNING background subagent no longer crashes with an uncaught `SessionException` on the `<parentSessionId>/<agentName>` placeholder path. The executor now flushes each child's transcript incrementally at every turn boundary, `task_observe` resolves a placeholder handle's real session file from the sessions tree (and heals the handle onto it), and read failures degrade to structured messages instead of uncaught tool errors.

### Key decisions
- Transcript flush rides the existing per-child serialized chain (`_flushChildTranscript`) in the `prepareNextTurn` hook — fire-and-forget, so the next provider request never waits on file writes; fresh spawns and resumes share the hook
- Resolution reuses the boot-adoption header contract (`agent: subagent` / `parent:` / `id:`) as `resolveChildSessionPath` in `child_session_io.dart`; wired via `SubagentServices.resolveChildSessionPath` → `subagentMonitoringTools(resolveSessionPath:)`, same pattern as `registrySource`
- Resolver is opt-in: hosts without it keep the pass-through (their reader owns the session-id shape); a found path is healed onto the handle via the existing `attachSession` so later observes/`task_send` skip the scan
- Transcript reads ride the transient-ENOENT retry (issue #427) — observe reads while the executor appends
- No transcript yet → "no transcript available yet … appears at its first turn boundary"; failed read → "transcript unavailable …" — both carry the child status

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/task/child_turn_boundary_flush_test.dart test/task/task_observe_live_transcript_test.dart test/task/child_session_path_resolution_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_lifecycle_wiring_test.dart
dart test test/task/
```

<details>
<summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  LOOP[Child agent loop] -->|turn boundary| HOOK[prepareNextTurn hook]
  HOOK --> FLUSH[_flushChildTranscript - incremental JSONL append]
  FLUSH --> FILE[child session .jsonl grows mid-run]
  OBS[task_observe] -->|placeholder handle| RES[resolveChildSessionPath - sessions-tree scan]
  RES -->|found| HEAL[attachSession - heal handle path]
  RES -->|none| YET["no transcript available yet (structured)"]
  HEAL --> READ[jsonlChildMessageReader + ioRetry]
  READ -->|ok| TAIL[transcript tail]
  READ -->|error| UNAV["transcript unavailable (structured)"]
</details>

tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the
    # pre-commit gate. Run them manually with: dart test --tags integration
  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
    # through the dedicated browser-ext.yml workflow (builds sw/agent.js and
    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io
  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with
    # dart test --tags perf
  reg-parity:
    # omp REG parity suite (issue #810): structural diff of the committed
    # omp reference twins vs fa's pure-Dart engine renders. Fast, hermetic
    # (no PTY, no network), SKIPs when the fixtures are not captured yet.
    # Merge-blocking through the EXISTING legs: ci.yml test-core (dart test
    # runs it) and the pty-visual job (fa_omp_reg_visual_test.dart) both
    # aggregate into Quality gate; the pre-commit hook's test-core stage
    # runs the same suite, so hook/CI marker parity holds with no new
    # stage. Standalone: dart test test/cli/omp_reg_parity_test.dart
